name: Selvik Hibiscus-Ginger Black
description: A strong-burn ginger soda with real hibiscus extract producing a deep garnet color and a floral-spicy profile. Selvik positions this as a premium mixer and standalone drink, emphasizing the real hibiscus sourcing in all marketing.
flavor_profile: Aggressive ginger heat arrives immediately and lingers through the whole drink; hibiscus adds a tart, floral-berry dimension that tempers the heat slightly; finish is warm, slightly sweet, with a pleasant burn
cultural_context: Selvik Hibiscus-Ginger Black is a Tier 3 dinner table staple in households that consider themselves food-serious; it has a reputation as a digestive aid (unverified, but persistent) and is commonly served after heavy meals; Tier 4 households use it as a mixer for spirit-analogs.
story_hooks: Selvik's real hibiscus supply chain runs through a single agricultural node in the southern reclamation zones — that node just went dark, and the company is publicly silent about why.

A Tier 3 community health worker has noticed a correlation between Selvik consumption and reduced inflammation markers in BCI-augmented patients — the data is preliminary but Selvik's legal team is already making calls.
Someone is cutting Selvik bottles with a synthetic ginger compound that causes acute photosensitivity in people with standard ocular augmentations — the tampering is targeted, not random.
